name: Nexus AI Production System
tag: A reference production AI stack that shows how ingestion, retrieval, memory, routing and monitoring fit together.

scenarios.title: Size a knowledge assistant
scenarios.ask: Size the stack for an internal assistant over {docs} thousand documents with {users} daily users.
steps: Ingestion
Plans to split {docs} thousand documents into about {=docs * 12} thousand chunks with metadata.
Retrieval
Hybrid search: keyword plus vector. Index size about {=round(docs * 12 * 3.1 / 1000, 1)} GB.
Memory
Per-user conversation memory with a 30-day limit.
Router
Sends simple lookups to a small model and complex questions to a larger one, about a 70 to 30 split.
Observability
Traces every request: retrieval hits, model used, latency and cost.
followups: Most questions are simple lookups. Sending those to a small model cuts cost a lot while keeping the larger model for questions that need it.
Daily questions spread over an 8-hour workday, times 3 for busy moments. Real traffic data will refine it.

scenarios.title: Find why answers got worse
scenarios.ask: User ratings dropped from {before} to {after} out of 5 this week. Trace the cause.
steps: Observability
Compared traces for low-rated answers this week and last week.
Retrieval check
Retrieval hit rate fell from 82% to 61% on Monday.
Ingestion check
Monday's document sync changed file formats, and {=round(abs(before - after) * 400)} documents were indexed without their text.
Fix plan
Re-index the affected files and add a check that blocks empty chunks.
followups: When answers get worse suddenly, the cause is more often the data the model sees than the model itself. Traces show that quickly.
Yes. An alert on retrieval hit rate would have fired on Monday morning. The fix plan adds it.

scenarios.title: Cut monthly AI costs
scenarios.ask: We spend ${spend} a month on model calls. Show where the stack can save.
steps: Observability
Grouped last month's calls by route and model.
Cache planner
{repeat}% of questions repeat within a day. A response cache would skip most of those calls.
Router tuner
Found that 20% of calls sent to the large model were simple enough for the small one.
Prompt trimmer
Shortened the system prompt by 35% with no drop in test scores.
followups: Will the cache give stale answers?
Cached answers expire after a set time and are cleared when the source documents change.
They are estimates from last month's traffic. The plan tracks actual spend weekly after each change.
